Southern Brave (SOB) takes on MI London (MIL) in Match No. 9 of the Hundred Men's 2026 at The Rose Bowl in Southampton on Monday, July 27. Both teams are coming off losses in their recent matches.

The Brave have started their campaign with two losses and suffered a nervy 5-run defeat to the Sunrisers Leeds at Headingley. They conceded a total of 187 for 5 in their 100 balls after bowling first, and missed out on the total despite runs from Jamie Smith, Ben McKinney and Tristan Stubbs.

MI London started their campaign off with a victory against the Sunrisers, but were beaten by the Welsh Fire in Cardiff, losing by 60 runs. They conceded a total of 167 for 5 courtesy of a stellar 98 from Rachin Ravindra. They were unable to chase the total despite James Vince's 66 at the top, losing by 15 runs.

The Rose Bowl in Southampton produced a slower wicket in the season's opening game between the Brave and the Welsh Fire. The surface is expected to play true but on the slower end, with batters needing to bide their time to score. Spinners should play a significant role given the grip and turn available.

Probable Southern Brave XI: Jamie Smith (wk), Ben McKinney, Marcus Stoinis, David Miller, Tristan Stubbs, Nikhil Chaudhary, Chris Jordan (capt), Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid, Luke Wood, Dan Worrall.

Probable MI London XI: Will Jacks, James Vince, Jason Roy, Sam Curran (capt), Nicholas Pooran (wk), Sherfane Rutherford, Tom Curran, Rashid Khan, Trent Boult, Richard Gleeson, Nathan Sowter.

MI London's Nicholas Pooran comes into this clash in fine form, having struck an unbeaten 22-ball 58 in the opening match against Sunrisers Leeds. The southpaw was quiet against Welsh Fire but is expected to have a significant impact in this encounter.

England veteran leg-spinner Adil Rashid showed his class against the Sunrisers, breaking the game open with three wickets in five balls. Rashid's flight and deception could trouble batters on a surface that offers turn, making him a key player for the Brave.

Match conditions favour cautious batting early on, with powerplay scores possibly lower than on flatter tracks. Teams that use spin effectively and time their acceleration in the middle overs should come out on top. Toss and final XI decisions will be crucial given the surface characteristics.
